item.title: A new butterfly in the meadow: magnetic lattice graphs with a circulant vertex coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.10767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the spectrum of quantum square lattice graph exposed to a homogeneous magnetic field with a rational flux through plaquette, assuming all nontrivial cases of the vertex coupling which is circulant and scale-invariant, with a particular attention to those of them that give rise to a dynamics violating the time reversal invariance. Except for two cases with partially decoupled edges, the remaining twelve split into two spectral classes; the second one offers a hitherto unknown butterfly pattern.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Exner, Jan Peka\v{r}

item.title: Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
item.description: arXiv:2611.11250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.
item.dc:creator: Durvudkhan Suragan

item.title: Root sharing and $2$-adic interpolation for Legendre polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.09312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stieltjes's conjecture on Legendre polynomials asserts that no two distinct Legendre polynomials can share a nonzero root. This question is, surprisingly, connected to a number of disparate mathematical areas. From the point of view of spectral geometry, this question concerns zero-sets of spherical harmonics. A disk counterpart to the conjecture is a famous theorem of Siegel on nonexistence of nonzero common roots of Bessel functions, proved using transcendence theory. A weak version of the conjecture is implied by the dynamical Mordell--Lang conjecture. We prove, using a $2$-adic analytic approach \`a la Skolem, that for a root $\alpha\neq 0$ of $P_l$ the set $\{n\in \mathbb{N}:\ P_n(\alpha)=0\}$ has cardinality at most $2l$. In particular, this set is finite.
item.dc:creator: Borys Kadets, Dan Mangoubi

item.title: The Fast Tree Transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.10466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Fast Tree Transform is a locally-aggregated transform defined for arbitrary graph geometries that generalizes both the Hadamard frequency transform and the Haar wavelet transform on the circle. The pure frequency part of the transform approximately diagonalizes the graph Laplacian; this fact makes it useful as a preconditioner in geometric optimization problems. The full transform provides an only slightly-redundant representation of signals on the graph that allows sparse representation of signals that include both edges and textures.
item.dc:creator: Paul Burchard

item.title: Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.12272v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the subellipticity of the analytically deformed Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and give two definitions of resonances, one based on analytic dilation and the other on analytic distortion in the $x$-variables. Due to the failure of global subellipticity of the distorted operator in dimensions $n \geq 2$, the second method can only be used in dimension one. We show that, whenever both methods are applicable, they give rise to the same set of resonances. We also prove that, when $|\na V(x)| = O(\w x^{-\rho})$ with $\rho>1$, positive resonances are embedded eigenvalues and/or scattering resonances whose resonant states belong to weighted $L^2$-spaces and satisfy an outgoing radiation condition.
item.dc:creator: Xue Ping Wang (LMJL)

item.title: High-energy eigenfunctions of point-perturbations of the Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2601.19705v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we explore the high-frequency properties of eigenfunctions of point perturbations of the Laplacian on a compact Riemannian manifold. These systems cannot be obtained as the quantization of a classical Hamiltonian, as the effect of the perturbation amounts to prescribing certain boundary conditions on a discrete set of points. We are interested in understanding to what extent the high-frequency behavior of eigenfunctions is governed by the global dynamics of the geodesic flow in the manifold (the classical flow corresponding to the unperturbed Laplacian). We prove that as soon as the Laplacian is perturbed by a finite set of point scatterers satisfying a \emph{non-focality} condition, namely, that the family of geodesics starting from this set and coming back to it has zero measure, semiclassical measures corresponding to high-frequency sequences of eigenfunctions are invariant under the geodesic flow. Invariance may fail when the non-focality condition does not hold, as is shown in a companion article [arXiv:2601.19701]. Our results are based on a quasimode construction that requires improved estimates on the spectral function of the Laplacian on the set of scatterers.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Verdasco

item.title: Applications of a Commutation Formula II
item.description: arXiv:2609.27151v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The principal {\it commutation formula} underlying the paper by Deift [24], is of the type \[ - z (AB - z I)^{-1} + A (BA - z I)^{-1} B = I, \quad z \in [\rho(AB) \cap \rho(BA)]\backslash\{0\}, \] where, temporarily, and for simplicity only, $A,B$ represent bounded operators in a Banach space. A fundamental consequence of this commutation formula is the fact that $AB$ and $BA$ are {\it essentially isospecral} in the sense that \[ \sigma(AB) \backslash \{0\} = \sigma(BA) \backslash \{0\}. \] Moreover, under appropriate trace class hypotheses, this implies the fundamental identity for (Fredholm) determinants \[ \det(I - AB) = \det(I - BA), \] which extends to modified (or regularized) Fredholm determinants. In this paper we briefly recall some of the applications of these commutation formulas to isospectrality, integrable systems, regularization of PDEs, and estimates in Statistical Mechanics and Quantum Field Theory discussed in [24]. Subsequently, we review some of the ramifications of commutation formulas that were established over the past fifty years, including determinants and dimension reduction, random matrix theory and dimension expansion, integrable operators, Poncelet's porism, interpolation, eigenvalue computation, KPZ, Pfaffians, the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation, one-dimensional scattering theory, Floquet theory, and the Miura transformation connecting the KdV and mKdV hierarchies.
item.dc:creator: Percy Deift, Fritz Gesztesy

item.title: Graph Fourier Neural Kernels: Learning Full PDE Trajectories Across Geometries and Anisotropic Parameter Fields
item.description: arXiv:2410.04655v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: High-fidelity simulations of time-dependent nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) are expensive to repeat across families of domains and parameter fields, a cost that recurs in design optimization, uncertainty quantification, and computational medicine. Most neural-operator surrogates require each domain to be mapped onto a common grid or reference shape, and few predict the full time course. We introduce Graph Fourier Neural Kernels (G-FuNK), a neural operator for second-order semilinear PDEs with a diffusive principal part that transfers across geometries and anisotropic diffusion tensors without coordinate maps or diffeomorphisms. A weighted graph and its Laplacian supply a spectral basis that encodes geometry and anisotropy. Shared layers act in this basis, at a cost linear in mesh size after one partial eigendecomposition per geometry, and a neural ODE integrator propagates the learned generator to full spatiotemporal trajectories on unseen domains. Across anisotropic heat flow, stiff reaction-diffusion, FitzHugh-Nagumo, and patient-specific left-atrial electrophysiology on CT-derived surfaces, G-FuNK reproduces held-out trajectories with relative $L^2$ error between 0.046 and 0.160. Its accuracy is comparable to that of a geometry-aware Fourier neural operator on regular domains, and its predictions are unchanged when a rectangular domain is rotated. On left atria, whose venous and valvular openings prevent mapping onto a reference shape, it predicts an 85-ms trajectory in under half a second, against about 5 minutes for finite elements, with a mean activation-time error of 1.73 ms. Accuracy depends on graph construction and is highest when the learned generator is integrated at its training time step.
item.dc:creator: Shane E. Loeffler, Zan Ahmad, Shiyi Chen, Syed Yusuf Ali, Carolyna Yamamoto, Kensuke Sakata, Dan M. Popescu, Alana Yee, Yash Lal, Natalia Trayanova, Mauro Maggioni

item.title: Spectral Graph Sparsification Preserves Representation Geometry in Graph Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2605.01136v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spectral graph sparsification is a classical tool for reducing graph complexity while preserving Laplacian quadratic forms. In graph neural networks (GNNs), sparsification is often used to accelerate computation while maintaining predictive performance. In this work, we study a complementary representation-level question: does sparsification preserve the geometry of learned embeddings? For polynomial-filter GNNs, we prove that any $\epsilon$-spectral sparsifier induces $O(\epsilon)$ perturbations in polynomial graph filters, multilayer hidden representations, and their Gram matrices. These guarantees imply stability of squared pairwise distances, class means, and covariance structure in embedding space. We further establish finite-time training stability: under smoothness and boundedness assumptions, gradient descent on dense and sparsified graphs produces weight trajectories whose separation grows at most proportionally to the sparsification distortion. Empirically, effective-resistance sparsification validates the predicted perturbation chain on synthetic graphs and preserves hidden representation geometry on real datasets. In our experiments, the gram matrix and training dynamics show low divergence even under substantial sparsification, consistent with the predicted stability under spectral sparsification. Hidden Gram preservation strongly predicts neighborhood preservation and class-centroid stability across FashionMNIST, Cora, and Paul15. Together, these results show that spectral sparsification preserves not only graph operators, but also the representation geometry that supports downstream use of GNN embeddings for interpretability.
item.dc:creator: Sanjukta Krishnagopal

item.title: A Dimension-Free Bound on the Poincar\'e Constant of Isotropic Log-Concave Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.07728v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits (KLS) conjecture asserts that isotropic log-concave probability measures have Poincar\'e constants bounded by a universal constant, independently of dimension. In this work, we provide a deterministic variational proof that the Poincar\'e constant $C_P(\mu)\le25$, where $\mu$ is any isotropic log-concave probability measure. The proof centers on mean-zero integration of compatible symmetric tensor fields. Starting from constant tensors, we obtain factorially normalized Appell polynomials by iterating this procedure. Using moment estimates and a quadratic variance inequality, we establish geometric bounds on these iterated primitives through a \emph{joint} variational argument over the measure and test function. At a maximizing pair, stationarity in the test function controls the weighted sum of the two highest-order cumulant terms arising from the measure variation. To extend these bounds to arbitrary compatible fields, we use a weighted Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition of weighted divergence, the formal adjoint of differentiation. Controlling the curl in the decomposition yields a curvature comparison for the integration operators, uniformly in tensor order. Combining this comparison with the Appell bounds gives a bound on the full integration operator and hence the stated Poincar\'e inequality. The estimate is independent of the auxiliary positive curvature, allowing approximation to general isotropic log-concave measures.
item.dc:creator: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Shiva Kasiviswanathan

item.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.35651v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$. We also show that the energy index of every critical spherical catenoid in $\mathbb{H^3}$, that is, the index of the second variation of its energy, equals four; hence the inequality between the energy index and the spectral index conjectured by Medvedev for geodesic balls of $\mathbb{H^n}$ fails.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Dorofeev, Alexander Pigazzini
